steps: Lithuania: LKT, Media Support Fund, NGO Fund, SADM, VRM, URM calls, National Sports Agency, public health bureaus, municipalities
EU: ESF+, ERPF, Erasmus+, Creative Europe, CERV, European Solidarity Corps
Region: Nordplus, Nordic Culture Point, Interreg, Baltic Culture Fund, Nordic Council of Ministers
Donors: Swiss programme, EEA and Norway Grants, private and community funds
notes: The deck's map of funding sources in four groups.

steps: Organisation prepares its own application
Submits to the fund or programme administrator
Administrator selects and funds
notes: Example: LIFE applications go straight to the European Commission via the Funding & Tenders portal.

steps: Fund announces a call every year or several times a year
Organisation checks deadlines before planning
Organisation applies in the next round
notes: Example: Erasmus+ main KA210 and KA220 deadline passed in March 2026, so most fields prepare for 2027.

steps: Main beneficiary is designated in advance
It runs partnerships, procurement or separate calls
Other organisations join as partners, suppliers or sub-call winners
notes: Example: a large share of the Swiss-Lithuanian programme goes through pre-defined projects.

steps: Organisation secures international funding or plans its budget
A fund covers only part of the budget, or tops up the funding already secured
Organisation covers the rest from its own funds
notes: Ask early whether you can contribute your own funds.

flow: EU programmes: how calls reach applicants
steps: ESF+ and ERPF: national calls
Erasmus+: direct and national calls
Creative Europe and CERV: direct European Commission calls
Interreg: calls run by each programme
notes: Summary of delivery channels for EU programmes relevant to several sectors.

steps: ESF-funded project AID2 run by ESFA
ESFA opens selection of project ideas (from 23 March 2026)
Public and private legal entities submit ideas via a form
Selected organisations contribute to the AID2 goal
notes: Goal: help socially vulnerable and excluded people enter the labour market.

steps: EU Erasmus+ programme
Youth Affairs Agency (JRA) administers the youth field in Lithuania
JRA publishes calls and application forms
Organisations apply by the deadline
notes: 2026 second or third round deadline: 1 October 2026.

steps: ERDF: about 10 billion EUR for Interreg across the EU in 2021-2027
Seven Interreg programmes open to Lithuanian participants
Each programme runs its own calls
Lead beneficiary (public body or NGO) applies with partners, private partners allowed
notes: Central Baltic also runs Small Project Proposals open to SMEs.

flow: EEA and Norway Grants 2021-2028 in Lithuania
steps: Donor states allocate 117.85 million EUR to Lithuania
Lithuania chose two main national programmes: Civil Protection (46 million EUR) and Justice (43.7 million EUR)
Donors reserve part of the funds for a Civil Society Fund
Civil Society Fund is administered by Atviros Lietuvos fondas, "OSFL Projektai" and the National Platform of NGDOs
NGOs apply to the Civil Society Fund
notes: Projects can run until 2031.

steps: Swiss-Europe Contribution
Swiss-Lithuanian programme with three areas
CPVA publishes calls
Large share delivered through pre-defined projects
notes: Areas: mother and child health and well-being; vocational education and training; civic engagement.

steps: Each municipality runs a Public Health Promotion Special Programme
Municipality announces a selection call for projects or measures
NGOs and communities apply
Municipality publishes the list of funded measures
notes: Examples: Klaipėda district (call of 2 March 2026), Vilnius city.

steps: Local Action Group (association of community and other NGOs, business and municipality representatives)
LAG announces local calls
NGOs registered in the LAG territory or local community organisations apply
notes: Rural and urban LAGs exist. The deck does not state where LAG funds come from.

steps: Find the call document (guidelines, funding conditions or competition regulations)
Read the selection criteria and what earns points
Check your commitments and the financial conditions
Check you have the team and partners
Justify the need with data and sources
Link problem, activities and results
Break the work down (WBS) and schedule it (Gantt)
Relevance and importance: the problem
Objectives and activities: the idea and how it is done
Results: the benefit
notes: Activities that do not answer a stated problem break the chain.

steps: Level 1: main project phases
Level 2: parts of each phase
Level 3: detailed work packages
notes: Example phases: preparation, design, implementation, testing and handover.

steps: Administration costs: administrator, accountant, admin communication, premises and utilities, other (bank fees)
Implementation costs: team salaries, external experts, team communication, travel, services, goods
Indirect costs: check whether the call allows them
Set the hourly rate including employer taxes and note its basis
Multiply by planned hours for the project period
Multiply by 1.0862 or 1.1101 for leave compensation
Record the result as the workplace cost
notes: Example: 15 EUR/h x 200 h = 3,000 EUR; x 1.0862 = 3,258.60 EUR.

flow: Justifying a service or goods line
steps: Name the item
State quantity (hours, days, months, km, participants)
State the unit rate and its source
Show the calculation
notes: Example: accounting 100 EUR/month x 10 months = 1,000 EUR, based on a past invoice.

steps: Cash: earned income, 1.2% income tax donations, business support, membership fees, municipal co-financing
In-kind: volunteer hours valued at a justified hourly rate
Contract and acceptance act for services
Invoice
Internal order where needed (for example travel)
Payroll records (contract, job description, timesheet, payroll sheet)
Travel documents
Count staff in annual work units
Check annual turnover or balance sheet total
Add partner and linked enterprises
Compare with micro, small and medium thresholds
Look at the reporting year and the two previous years
2021-2027 EU investments are split between the Capital region (SR) and Central and Western Lithuania (VVL)
Calls then set separate SR and VVL budgets
Your project draws on the envelope for its region
notes: SR 235.5 million EUR, VVL 896.6 million EUR.

steps: Check age, registration and competence requirements
Apply to NMA within the call window, or before the budget runs out
Receive a preferential loan of up to 100,000 EUR covering up to 100% of eligible costs
notes: Legal persons meeting the age and competence rules can also apply.

flow: Applying for an agricultural or rural investment measure
steps: Update your data in public registers
Confirm no debts to the state budget or Sodra
Fill applicant and project information
List eligible costs with 3 comparable offers each
Set financing sources equal to the value with VAT
Declare fixed assets and land
Justify innovativeness
Set realistic monitoring indicators
Accept commitments, sign the declaration and all data consents
Attach a business plan if the measure requires it
notes: Given in the deck after the NMA and local action group sections.
